newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOTORCYCLING-CHAMPION DOOHAN EARNS HIS SECOND WIN OF THE SEASON.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-CHAMPION DOOHAN EARNS HIS SECOND WIN OF THE SEASON.

text.p: Reigning 500cc world champion Michael Doohan of Australia clinched his second victory of the season in a hard-fought battle at the Japanese motorcycling Grand Prix on Sunday.
Doohan, who started second on the grid, was engaged in a neck-and-neck battle until the very end with his team mates at Repsol Honda, Alex Criville from Spain and Tadayuki Okada from Japan.
After passing pole position starter Okada on the 10th lap, Doohan kept the lead for the rest of the race. The Australian set a record of two minutes 7.782 seconds on the eighth lap.
Doohan finished the 21 laps in 45 minutes 11.995 seconds, followed by Criville who finished half a second later in 45:12.426. Okada came in third with 45:18.042.
"I could hear him (Criville) at every turn," said Doohan. "He was trying but I tried to be as smooth as possible and stay in front."
Criville, who also placed second at the Malaysian Grand Prix last week, said, "I tried to pass Mick at the last lap but Mick was riding very, very well...I'm happy with second. I'm okay."
Sunday was also a victory for Honda, which had won only one previous race at its home ground, with Doohan in 1992.
Doohan keeps first place in the world championship standings with 50 points, followed by Criville on 40. Honda top the constructors' championship with 50 points.
Japanese riders dominated the podium in the other classes.
Daijiro Kato marked his first victory in the 250cc category with a time of 41:42.226. His compatriot Toru Ukawa came in second.
Italian world champion Max Biaggi managed seventh place on his Honda despite a dislocated shoulder.

"I can hardly believe I got seventh", said Biaggi, who was injured when he crashed during qualifying on Friday. "The pain in my shoulder was just about unbearable, especially when braking. Maybe I took too many risks but that's the way I am."
Japan's Noboru Ueda won the 125cc category with a time of 41:48.072.
